reviews.comment: Don't listen to the hate. He is not a 1 star prof. He does care about his students success, but you have to put in the work to understand his notes, because he thinks differently than most so they're a little messy. Exams are straightforward with nothing that's not on the notes/homework. Homework solutions are posted and very helpful for studying.

Whitcomb despite the hate, cares about his students and if you put in the effort, he will help you. His notes are a little confusing but once you decipher them, they can become very useful. Exams are conceptual and there aren't that many curveballs. Chill guy.

He gas a tendency to not actually teach a concept, just vaguely explain how to do it with words and no math, and make questions on exams where you just verbatim regurgitate whatever he says and any slight variation is a loss of 5-15 points. That basically sums the experience of his class, its not hard but boy is it annoying.

I have only taken him for a couple of weeks. He is very picky about assignments; he is unclear on any questions he gives during assignments; and when he gave practice problems he did not even explain how to do them; when he was giving lectures, I understood the method of how to do things, but he makes me understand even less making harder to learn.

He's single handedly the worst professor in the Aerospace department if not the entire university. Lectures have zero examples and he expects you to apply the material two seconds after he's explained it without giving any explanation on how the theory can be applied. Please avoid at all cost if you actually want to learn and be successful.
reviews.ratingTags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Try to take notes in class even though they are impossible to follow. The textbook isn't properly synced with the course material. Take advantage of the T.A as he is the only useful resource. He WILL lie that attendance means extra credit. The T.A. might say it's "different this semester". Don't believe him. Overall, AVOID AT ALL COST.
reviews.ratingTags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: Lecture is completely pointless as he teaches off of extremely hard to follow code with very little explanation. Due to this, homework's are complete nightmares taking up to 8hrs to learn the course material and apply it. The one good aspect is, if you do the homework, exams are extremely fair as and are almost identical to homework assignments.
reviews.ratingTags: Tough grader--Lots of homework--So many papers

reviews.comment: A man who despises examples and help, who also dislikes teaching it appeared as he would simply ramble for the entire class periods and read off his premade code and slides. While he isn't as rude as others, he simply zaps the fun out of engineering and dumbs it down to a slew of Matlab assignments and arbitrary exams to determine your success.
reviews.ratingTags: Tough grader--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Dr. Whitcomb saved me tens of thousands of dollars. Originally I wanted to get a PhD, but later came to the conclusion that it isn't worth it because then I'd have to work with people as god awful and pedagogically incompetent as him for the rest of my life. Allowing this man to teach any subject to anyone is a cardinal sin against the student body

While initially hopeful for the content of this course, Whitcomb's inability to clearly convey class material or answer questions, coupled with his complete disdain for examples makes him by far the worst professor I have had at this university.

JDW is the single best reason for abolishing tenure in the state of Texas. He should not be allowed to teach. This class was the first I've taken that made me seriously consider dropping out because of how horrendous he ran the class. The only thing your given are the schizophrenic ramblings he calls notes/lectures. Examples are rare
Expect to learn nothing and work hard.

This class is the most powerful anesthetic ever. Half of the class is asleep within 10 minutes, but they are the lucky ones. Those unfortunate enough to be awake are subjected to tangent ramblings and their questions are dodged and mocked. He refuses provide ANY example of how to solve problems and expects us to know material on first pass by magic

Whitcomb can't handle questions. If you ask him a question, he either will not understand, become defensive, or act like you should have just referenced the notes instead of asking him.
Furthermore, his teaching is very derivation-focused, but on the exam, he really wants you to memorize formulas and regurgitate formulas.
There are also stories...
Avoid.

Beware of the white-haired man. He doesn't answer questions properly. In fact, he doesn't like when you ask questions but he encourages you to ask anyway. He gaslights the entire class. He picks on students in class when we are minding our own business. He says something won't be on an exam and it's there anyway. Overall, terrible professor.

John Whitcomb has used the same lecture plans/fill-in notes for his entire teaching career. He has taught the same material so many times I do not even think he knows it himself. In addition to this, he flat-out lies to his students. He promises curves/drops based on attendance but does not follow through. Avoid Whitcomb at all costs.
reviews.ratingTags: Tough grader--Lots of homework--So many papers

reviews.comment: He has no rules. No boundaries. He doesn't flinch at torture, human trafficking, or genocide. He's not loyal to a flag or country or any set of ideals. He trades blood for money. You don't want to know what it's cost already to put you next to him. It will cost you a piece of yourself.

John Whitcomb is a very frustrating professor to have. On one hand, he seems very passionate about what he talks about, but he isn't anywhere near as passionate about making sure you understand the content. He couldn't handle any questions he was asked and never showed example problems. Our TA was a lot more helpful.

He is neat to talk to as long as you do not ask anything directly related to the class. HW is taken straight from lecture materials, tests are based on lectures and HW. Show up to office hours and labs. Introduce yourself, get to know him. It will go a long way. As far as 222 goes be ready to teach yourself and dig around the Internet.

When I had JDW for 222, he was horrible. But for 306, he seems to have taken the criticism. He works out problems, he is reasonable with homework, he always asks for feedback. Other than one chapter of the text, chapter 3, I found the book he has written to be incredibly helpful. Show up, go to office hrs, do the hw and you'll be okay. Good luck
reviews.ratingTags: Get ready to read--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: Whitcombs low rating is underserved imo. The easiest way to get an A in this class is to show up consistently and put in effort in the labs and hw. He sends out surveys to ask for feedback, but then will refuse to adapt most to the requests. He is reasonable with hw deadlines and is a good prof if he matches your learning style. If not, good luck.
Taking this class was not a good experience, would not recommend taking again. Lectures were not very helpful and a lot of this class was learning the material on your own.

The lectures are based on the textbook (he wrote it) and his answers to any questions are brief and come across as derogatory.  His homework and exams are graded very strictly. He gets angry when people don't go to class/understand the material.  The homework is difficult and your primary resource is the textbook which is very hard to understand.

His test and homework are not that hard if you know the material. With that said, he doesn't provide enough material to study off with (he wrote his own textbook which is just awful to read). I advise you to avoid him at all costs if you really want to learn. Earned B above taking the same course through another profs while he gave a C or below.
reviews.ratingTags: Tough grader--Lots of homework--Beware of pop quizzes

reviews.comment: *AERO 222, Whitcomb lacks any and all ability communicate and should never be entrusted with instructing students for the rest of his natural life. He is oblivious to his teaching problems and will blame anything including the TAs who try to help students as problems in the class. The entire concept of tenure is challenged by this man's existence.

The TA sent out a survey to all the students asking them to rate their understanding of the subjects 'taught' by Dr. Whitcomb so far, and after all the sections responded with a resounding 'unsatisfactory' understanding of these subjects, Dr. Whitcomb got the TA removed from instructing for his class. This guy could not be a worse instructor.
Graduating late is better than taking this class
reviews.ratingTags: Lots of homework--Get ready to read--Tough grader

reviews.comment: Complains about students flaws constantly, but fails to reflect on the poor quality of his teaching and the hostile environment he creates in the lectures.
reviews.ratingTags: Graded by few things--Test heavy--Tough grader

reviews.comment: Does not care about teaching, only complains about students being absent. You can get the right answer and get no credit. He made us write an essay about why other students are missing class
reviews.ratingTags: Graded by few things--Beware of pop quizzes--Tough grader

reviews.comment: Dr. Whitcomb is a tough and at times pugnacious professor. Expect a lot of homework, although solutions are provided, as well as pop quizzes. Be sure to "stay up" as he always says. Exams are similar to sample questions he provides and old exams. Get ready to argue for points back if you want to pass.
reviews.ratingTags: Lots of homework--Beware of pop quizzes--Tough grader

reviews.comment: No details and extra explanation in class. No process credits in exam. Huge work of self reading required because the professor doesn't like tell you details. The professor is not helpful because he always said 'its not a math class. '
He does not curve.
